newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar ends at two-week highs, funds buy.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar ends at two-week highs, funds buy.

text.p: CSCE world sugar futures closed at two week highs on Wednesday amid brisk chart-driven fund buying, dealers said.
The benchmark October contract rose to 11.34 cents, its highest level since reaching 11.40 cents on July 1, while several of the back months surged to new life-of-contract highs.

The October contract closed at 11.30 cents, having ranged from 11.34 to 10.96 cents. Second-position March settled up 0.31 at 11.47 cents while the rest of the board finished 0.25 to 0.15 cent higher.

Early in the day, October dipped to 10.96 cents where trade buying emerged to buoy the contract over unchanged. Fund buying came in above 11.12 cents and continued to erode trade selling overhead, dealers said.
Despite the close just under the day's highs, market sources expect prices to ease on Thursday amid profit-taking. Firm resistance was seen at 11.35 cents in October followed by 11.50 cents.
A neutral to bearish fundamental picture should also limit gains, analysts said.

"Because this was chart-driven buying the market is vulnerable to profit taking," Refco analyst Ann Prendergast said. "I don't see any fundamental grounds for a substantial price rise," she added, pointing to a surplus of Brazilian sugar.

Analysts said Tuesday's move below key 11.00 cents was expected to attract follow-through selling and pressure the market to its next downside target of 10.80 cents. Instead, the chartists viewed the move down as a buying opportunity, which fueled today's sharp rise.
An estimated 33,951 lots changed hands on the day, compared with Tuesday's official 21,472 lots.
Open interest in the benchmark October contract fell by 2,014 lots to 90,349 lots as of Wednesday. March gained 923 contracts to stand at 43,745 lots.
